title: Automatic per-model compilation tuning and stable pinning for MHA / GQA / MoE
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Goal: Extend the model onboarder to automatically generate, validate, and publish compilation + kernel-selection profiles for new model variants (MHA, GQA, MoE) and provide a stable pinning mechanism that ties a model version to a certified profile. This reduces flakiness from autotuning regression and enables safe rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope:
- Autoscan incoming model artifacts and infer architecture (MHA/GQA/MoE) and shard/parallelism config.
- Run deterministic compile runs with three candidate kernel sets: low-latency, cost-optimized, and fallback-safe.
- Telemetry harness to benchmark candidates on representative micro-benchmarks (sequence lengths, batch mix) pulled from historical workload fingerprints.
- Publish vetted profile JSONs to the model catalog with metadata: profile_id, metric_summary, compile_commit, hardware_compatibility.
- Create pin API allowing customers and internal routing policies to reference profile pins (model@v1.2 -> profile_id).
- Rollout strategy: canary with gradual percentage, automatic automatic rollback if p99 latency or error rate regresses beyond thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Onboarder produces at least one validated profile per new model type within CI / nightly pipeline.
- Profile publishing workflow includes automated signature and changelog entry.
- Console displays profile health and pin mapping per model.
- Canary rollout executed via routing policy and can be reverted automatically when thresholds breached.

Out of scope: full kernel autotuner UX and per-token micro-optimizer changes (follow-up ticket).
tasks: Benchmark harness that replays representative sequences
Publish profile to catalog with metadata and changelog
Implement profile pin API and storage
comments: 2026-02-22 - Marco Ruiz: Kicked off initial spike. Created prototype classifier using model config heuristics; it reliably distinguishes GQA vs MHA for our test suite (10/10). Next: wire into CI.

2026-02-26 - Asha Patel: Spiked a three-mode compile job on a 4xA100 pool; latency profile reduces p50 by ~12% for MHA-24B but increases p99 slightly due to batch packing. Need to add KV cache warmup scenario to benchmarks.

2026-03-02 - Taylor Nguyen (code review): Left feedback on publish API security surface; we should sign profiles with build CI key and add an allowlist for profile consumption in Private deployments. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarder/pull/78

2026-03-05 - Product (Leila Morgan): Confirmed console UX requirements; prefer 'profile health' to include cost delta, latency delta, and regression flags. Linking doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/Profile+Publishing+Spec

2026-03-09 - SRE (Ethan Cole): Proposed rollout thresholds: fail if p99 increases >15% on canary or error_rate increases >0.5%. Also requested circuit-breaker to pause rollouts when infra utilization >85%.

2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Implemented profile metadata schema and basic publish endpoint. Demoed metadata blob to team; next is hooking telemetry harness and automatic signing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarder/pull/102
notes: We're intentionally conservative for MoE: compile candidates must include a shard-aware kernel and a fallback path that avoids cross-expert synchronizations. GQA experiments show different batching behavior; test vectors must include grouped-query patterns. Expect follow-up RNAs for per-hardware micro-optimizations.
